hypothesis: Bounded canonical loops with serial, nested, asymmetric or cross-edge branch-only producers can be split before original-loop vectorization legality when their integer-add or ordered float/double-add recurrences update unconditionally at the unique latch. A linear acyclic-CFG proof admits these producers without if-conversion or a VPlan for the original loop. The producer can remain scalar while ordinary LV independently selects the consumer VF. Single-block, single triangle/diamond and narrow compact-participation support are retained. There is no new profitability model, pressure/chain-depth/reduction-count threshold, numerical relaxation or original-loop vectorizability prerequisite.
semantics: For multiblock loops, hasAcyclicProducerCFG requires a unique exiting latch and BranchInst terminators. All non-latch successor edges must stay in the loop and cannot target its header. It counts incoming edges with the latch backedge/exit excluded, then performs an iterative Kahn traversal seeded only by the header. Visiting every loop block proves both reachability and absence of internal cycles. Every non-latch node has a successor in this finite DAG, so the latch is the only sink: every iteration reaches it exactly once. Duplicate successor edges are counted/decremented separately. Single-block loops retain the old fast path and later exit diagnostics. Existing simplify-form, dedicated-exit, LCSSA, unique-exit, canonical-zero/one-IV, invariant equality-bound and finite SCEV trip checks still apply. Newly admitted unconditional updates must reside in the latch; existing narrow header-update cases remain supported. Conditional backedge PHIs require the unchanged single triangle/diamond recognizer before participation analysis, so a two-input merge in a larger serial/nested CFG cannot acquire a counter that assumes one participation arm. All rejections precede mutation. Emission is unchanged: original branches, contribution PHIs, arm-local loads/divisions and safe helper calls remain in place, with distinct available contribution values stored at the latch under the original iteration index. Consumer updates are cloned, preserving add flags, FP operand order and per-reduction iteration order. No inactive zero arithmetic or speculative arm evaluation is introduced. Header/update use restrictions preserve reduction-feedback rejection, and only final reduction results may escape through the original exit. Other live-outs, stores, volatile/atomic accesses, unsupported instructions and unsafe calls remain rejected. Calls still require the explicit direct memory(none), nounwind, willreturn, speculatable and other existing effect contracts; no libm-name or errno assumptions are added. Input/output aliasing and enclosing-loop row stores retain their original producer/consumer sequencing. Ordinary ordered FP is unchanged under both settings of the separate fission FP-reordering option; strictfp functions and constrained FP remain rejected. Executable verification is requested through the extended existing checker, not claimed run. Three mixed acyclic producers and an enclosing-loop producer are compiled both as untouched original scalar IR and actual transformed stages, with independent C scalar formulas as a second reference. The checker verifies exact source-location Selected, producer VF 1, consumer VF vscale x 4, capacity/bytes, preserved producer edges/PHIs and arm-local operations, shared slots and ordered consumer reductions. Host-only probes are inserted after PHIs in exact producer header, latch, vector-consumer header and scalar tail. Expected visits are N, N, floor(N/VF), N%VF, summed per row for enclosing loops. Mixed cases exercise every N=0..65, invalid 66/UINT64_MAX, positive/negative nonzero divisors, all-load/all-division (null FP input), alternating phases, runs, sparse/random branches and nested branch combinations. Inputs are preserved, output canaries checked, and repeated/alias invocations compare integer and ordered non-NaN FP bits, signed zero included; NaNs compare by classification without inventing payload guarantees. Enclosing loops use zero/one/four and invalid rows, initial/carry/export state, exact stage visits, independent unaliased/aliased C references and future-row input aliasing. One and two ordinary LV invocations, both FP option settings and vscales 1/2/4/8/32 are covered. Additional actual scalar-stage comparisons execute 1, 255 and 16384 trips, including the full default scratch capacity, against original IR and independent formulas with exact producer/latch/consumer counts. Existing executable cases and correctness assertions are retained.
costs: Let M be the proven maximum trip count, N the actual count, and S the sum of allocation sizes of distinct contribution SSA values. Static entry scratch remains M*S plus existing ABI alignment padding, checked by existing unsigned arithmetic, IV representability, pointer-index bounds and the 65536-byte default per-candidate ceiling. It can reserve stack space even on a guarded bypass. Three mixed fixtures each use one 65*i32, one 65*double and one 65*float array for four reductions (shared integer contribution): 1044 accounted bytes including 4 padding bytes; logical stores 16*N bytes and loads 16*N bytes, total 32*N. The enclosing producer uses 784 accounted bytes (65*i32 plus 65*double and 4 padding bytes), reused across rows, with 12*N stores and 12*N loads per row. Capacity does not multiply by row count. Scalar boundary execution uses 4, 1020 and 65536 scratch bytes for M=1,255,16384; tests reject the 256-trip i8 overflow and 16385*i32 byte excess before mutation, and a 3-byte ceiling rejects every fixture in that boundary file. There are zero added original-input rereads, duplicated producer operations or recomputed contributions, no participation/mask arrays for these unconditional streams, and no new per-iteration producer branch or counter. Existing producer iteration guards stay in place; the existing extra consumer loop/control and ordinary LV vector/tail checks remain. There are no new alias or SCEV guards, unbounded/dynamic allocation, path enumeration, if-conversion or generic dependence machinery. The added admission check uses O(B+E) time and O(B) temporary compiler memory (E<=2B for branches), iterative rather than recursive; existing instruction/use scans, SCEV analysis and full-function dominator recalculation are unchanged. Narrow compact recognition remains a separate constant-size check. Host probes/reference formulas increase validation cost only and are excluded from RVV codegen inputs. Physical stack padding/cache traffic, register pressure and speedups have not been measured.
limitations: This worker ran no compiler, build, test runner, executable checker, parser fixture or try.sh. Only source/artifact inspection, file-generation/editing scripts and git diff --check were used. All new expectations and execution comparisons await the harness. Fixed-vscale scalar-remainder host execution is not RVV execution; default EVL/VP has IR/RVV machine verification only and is deliberately not specialized by the host checker. No RVV hardware/emulator execution or measured speedup is claimed. The ordinary loop worklist still generally admits only innermost loops; cyclic producers containing a natural subloop are normally skipped as outer targets. The rejection test additionally uses explicit outer-loop hints/native worklist to exercise the new acyclicity rejection at the original outer source location. This task does not widen that worklist. Newly admitted CFGs must be branch-only DAGs with unconditional latch adds; switches, internal cycles, early exits, header updates in larger CFGs, general conditional/multiple participation streams, non-add recurrences, unsupported live-outs and unsafe effects remain unsupported. Existing strict/constrained-FP rejection is unchanged. Scratch remains full-trip, bounded per candidate and untiled, without a whole-function stack cap. Source matcher/probes are fixture-specific verification, not a general IR proof. No immutable benchmark, harness, other worktree, common build checkout, Git index/history/ref or compiler binary was changed; unfinished d2 work was not integrated. No coverage, maturity or performance improvement on original corpus inputs is claimed before independent results.
test_expectations: Intentional change: the old reject_arm_cross_edge function is preserved verbatim as acyclic_cross_edge in the positive scalar-acyclic.ll fixture, with positive scalar/EVL/tail checks. It has one latch predecessor and satisfies the DAG proof; its rejection was solely the old narrow CFG shape restriction. All semantic rejection cases in the old file remain. New larger conditional serial/nested shapes still reject scalar-unsupported-cfg despite a two-input reduction merge. New header-update larger CFGs reject scalar-unsupported-recurrence. Source-location rejection checks cover early exits, reduction-dependent predicates/contributions, update observers, non-reduction live-outs, stores, unsafe calls, switch terminators and larger conditional shapes. The cyclic outer target has a separate native-worklist source-location check because the default worklist visits only its inner natural loop. Eligible original targets can now change from scalar-unsupported-cfg to Selected or a later specific rejection; diagnostic pass/name/location emission is untouched. Single-block exit diagnostics and existing narrow compact behavior are retained. No correctness assertion was removed or weakened.
